newsitem.title: INDIA: India speaker meets president on fate of budget.
newsitem.headline: India speaker meets president on fate of budget.

text.p: The speaker of India's parliament on Thursday met President Shankar Dayal Sharma ahead of a crucial trust vote to discuss the fate of the path-breaking budget for financial 1997/98 (April-March), officials said.
"Among other things, the speaker had discussions on the budget," an official at the presidential palace said.

"The speaker conveyed to the president that the country would face a constitutional breakdown if the Lok Sabha was dissolved without passing the budget for 1997/98," the Press Trust of India (PTI) reported.
The speaker, P.A. Sangma, met lawmakers from different political parties before meeting Sharma, the officials said.
Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's ruling coalition faces a confidence vote in the lower house of parliament or Lok Sabha, on Friday.

The fate of the market-friendly budget presented by Finance P. Chidambaram on February 28 was called into question on March 30 after the Congress party withdrew its make-or-break support for Deve Gowda's minority United Front coalition.
Sangma had told reporters last week it was up to government to decide when the budget would be put to a vote in parliament.
Parliament has to approve the budget before the end of May.
It was originally scheduled to be taken up for voting after parliament reconvened on April 21, but rapid political developments have forced in a special session on Friday.
Last month the lower house approved a vote on account, a bill that provides money to fund government programmes until the 1997/98 (April-March) budget is approved.
Most parties have agreed not to allow the political crisis to derail the budget.
They have offered different solutions to end the impasse, including a proposal to take up the discussion on the budget after the vote of confidence.
